The city of Aethelgard does not sit on the ocean; it floats above it, suspended by a lattice of massive, buoyant aerogel struts and magnetic levitation rings anchored to the seabed. Daily life here is defined by the constant, gentle sway of the waves below and the ever-present salt spray that coats every surface.
Mornings begin not with an alarm, but with the rhythmic creak of the city’s suspension cables adjusting to the tide. Residents wake in homes built into the underside of the floating platforms, where the ceiling is a transparent polymer looking down into the churning blue depths. Breakfast is often eaten on the "Underside Balconies," where the wind is strongest and the view of the open sea is unobstructed.
Transportation is vertical and horizontal. To move between districts, citizens use "Tide-Lifts," glass elevators that descend through the city’s hollow core to the lower decks, or ascend to the "Crown," the highest point where the air is cleaner and the sun hits first. For longer distances, small, silent electric skiffs glide along the water’s surface, tethered to the city’s perimeter by magnetic rails, allowing residents to commute without ever touching the ground.
